description: Build an eSIM plan to the traveller's liking for one destination: how much data, for how many days, optionally which network it runs on and whether calls and texts are bundled. Returns the one real plan that matches, with its id and live price, never a made-up combination: a shape nobody sells is snapped to the nearest one that is, one axis at a time, and every change is spelled out in `adjustments` so you can read it back. Use it when the traveller knows what they want ("10 GB on Docomo for two weeks"); use plan-trip when they want a recommendation or the trip has several countries. To buy, pass `plan.id` to get-checkout-link when a person is paying, or to create-checkout-session when you are. Read-only: it reserves nothing and charges nothing.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code of the destination, e.g. "JP". Look it up with list-destinations rather than guessing.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 three-letter code the price is quoted in, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP". Defaults to EUR. An unknown code falls back to EUR rather than failing.

data_mb.description: Data allowance wanted, in megabytes: 1 GB is 1024 MB, so 5 GB is 5120. Pass 0 for an unlimited plan. Snapped to the nearest size sold when no plan has exactly this size.

network.description: Optional. The mobile network the plan should run on, by carrier name as `options.networks` lists them, e.g. "NTT Docomo" or "au". Matching is case-insensitive and a single carrier of a multi-network plan is enough. Omit for the cheapest network.

validity_days.description: How many days the plan should stay valid, 1 to 365. Snapped to the nearest length sold for the chosen size.

voice.description: Optional. True to require a plan that bundles calls and texts. Defaults to false, data only. If no such plan exists the answer is data only and says so.

name: build-plan

adjustments.description: Every way the built plan differs from what was asked, one sentence each, written to be read to the traveller. Empty when the plan matches the request exactly.

built.description: The specification of the plan actually built, after any adjustment. Null when nothing was found.

data_mb.description: The data size of the plan built, in megabytes; 0 means unlimited.

network.description: The network of the plan built, or null for any network.

validity_days.description: The length of the plan built, in days.

voice.description: Whether calls and texts are bundled of the plan built.

found.description: True when a plan was built. False when the destination sells nothing at all, in which case `plan` is null.

options.description: What else could be asked for, so a follow-up question can be answered without another call.

data_mb.description: Every data size sold for the destination, in megabytes, metered ascending and 0 (unlimited) last.

networks.description: Every network the destination is sold on. Empty when no plan names its carrier.

network.description: The value to pass as `network` to choose this one.

network_generation.description: The fastest generation any plan on this network states. Null when none states one: not stated, not any generation.

validity_days.description: Every length sold for the size that was built, in days.

voice.description: True when at least one plan bundles calls and texts.

plan.description: The plan built: the same shape get-plan returns. Its `id` is what you buy with. Null when nothing was found.

carrier.description: The mobile network this plan runs on, when we can name it. Null when we cannot.

country.description: The one country this plan is filed under. Null for a regional or worldwide plan.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code the from_price_cents beside it is expressed in, which is the currency you asked for, e.g. "EUR". Null exactly when from_price_cents is null, which is what a country nested on a plan answers: nothing priced it there.

from_price_cents.description: Cheapest plan for this destination, in minor units (cents) of the response currency, so 1250 is 12.50. Null when this response did not price the destination.

description: Answer "does this eSIM plan work in X?" for one destination, as a yes or no rather than a country list. Takes a plan id and a destination (a country name or two-letter code). Reports whether the destination is covered, and separately whether it is explicitly excluded from an otherwise regional plan. Use get-plan-coverage when you need the full list of countries instead.

description: How much data an eSIM has used and how much is left, for one eSIM on a paid order. Identified by the order id and the email that bought it, plus the ICCID from get-order-status or get-esim-activation. Allowances are in megabytes. Readings are served from a cache refreshed every couple of minutes: checked_at says when the reading was taken. An unlimited plan reports its full-speed allowance for the current period rather than a total.

email.description: The email address the order was bought with.

iccid.description: The ICCID of the eSIM to read, as returned by get-order-status.

order_id.description: The order id from the buyer's confirmation email or order page.

name: check-esim-usage

activated_at.description: When the eSIM first connected, ISO 8601. Null before activation.

checked_at.description: When this reading was TAKEN, ISO 8601. Readings come from a cache refreshed every couple of minutes, so do not present the number as live.

data_remaining_mb.description: Megabytes left. NULL on an unmetered plan, which does not mean zero: it means the supplier reports no allowance to count down.

data_total_mb.description: Size of the current bundle in megabytes, reflecting any top-ups. Null on an unmetered plan.

data_used_mb.description: Megabytes used on the current bundle; 1 GB is 1024 MB.

expires_at.description: When the plan lapses, ISO 8601. Null when the supplier reports none.

iccid.description: The eSIM this reading belongs to.

is_unlimited.description: Whether the plan is sold as unlimited. Almost none are uncapped: see the period fields for what that actually means here.

percentage_remaining.description: Share of the bundle left, 0-100. Null on the same terms.

percentage_used.description: Share of the bundle spent, 0-100. Null on an unmetered plan, where there is no total to be a share of.

period_high_speed_mb.description: Size of that period allowance, so the figure above can be read as "945 MB of 3 GB left today".

period_reduced_speed_kbps.description: Speed the plan throttles to once the period allowance is spent. NULL means the data STOPS instead, which is a different thing to tell a traveller.

period_remaining_mb.description: Full-speed data left in the CURRENT reset period, for a plan whose allowance refills (say 3 GB a day). Null when the plan has no reset period. Deliberately separate from data_remaining_mb, which describes the whole plan.

period_reset.description: How often it refills: "daily", "weekly" or "monthly". Null when it does not.

status.description: eSIM state at the time of the reading, e.g. "active".

title: Check eSIM data usage

description: Open a checkout session for one or more eSIM plans at frozen prices, using the plan ids that plan-trip, list-plans or get-plan returned. Use it once the traveller has chosen what to buy. It CHARGES NOTHING and reserves no stock: it prices the basket, freezes those prices until the session's price_locked_until, and hands back the session plus a bearer agent key. Payment, completion and cancellation happen afterwards over the SimFuse agentic HTTP API with that key, as the session's `note` explains, and the eSIM is delivered by email once payment settles. Each call opens a NEW session and mints a NEW key, so call it once per basket rather than retrying it to re-read one.

agent_name.description: Optional. Name of the assistant or app opening the session, e.g. "Claude". Recorded on the agent key so we can tell integrations apart. Defaults to "mcp-client".

buyer_email.description: Optional but strongly recommended. The traveller's email address, where the eSIM and its installation details are sent once payment settles. Ask for it rather than inventing one.

currency.description: Optional. ISO 4217 three-letter code to price the session in, e.g. "USD", "EUR", "GBP". Defaults to EUR. Every amount in the answer is minor units (cents) of this currency.

items.description: What to buy: one entry per plan, 1 to 50 entries. Pass the whole basket in one call, e.g. [{"id":"01JVQ...","quantity":1}].

id.description: A plan id (26-character ULID) from plan-trip, list-plans, get-plan or the product feed, e.g. "01JVQ2S6D4X8N0RMB7YQZ5K3TA". Never invent one.

quantity.description: How many of this plan to buy, 1 to 20. One eSIM per unit, so 2 means two separate eSIMs of the same plan (one traveller normally needs 1).

name: create-checkout-session

agent_key.description: The bearer key for every follow-up call on this session, shown ONCE and never again. Send it as "Authorization: Bearer <key>". It is a credential: use it, do not read it out to the traveller.

api.description: The HTTP endpoints for this session, all taking the agent_key as a bearer token.

cancel.description: POST here to cancel the session.

complete.description: POST here to complete the purchase, which is where payment happens.

session.description: GET this to re-read the session and its current totals.

note.description: How to use the key and how long the prices hold. Worth following literally.

session.description: The priced checkout session, in the same shape the agentic HTTP API returns it.

buyer.description: The buyer, when one was given. Null when no email was supplied, in which case ask for one before completing.

handlers.description: The ways this session can be paid.

default_asset.description: Default asset for a crypto handler.

settlement.description: "synchronous" settles during completion; "asynchronous" settles later, so a 200 is not yet a purchase.

id.description: Handler id to name when completing the session.

requires_delegate_payment.description: Whether the agent must mint a delegated payment token first.

requires_pci_compliance.description: Whether card data passes through the agent.

currency.description: Lower-case ISO 4217 code every amount is in, e.g. "eur".

expires_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp after which this session can no longer be completed.

fulfillment_options.description: How the eSIM is delivered. Instant and free, stated explicitly so nobody has to guess whether shipping is coming.

description.description: What the traveller receives, and when.

amount.description: Amount in minor units (cents) of the session currency. A discount is NEGATIVE, so the lines sum to the total.

display_text.description: The line written for a person.

type.description: Always "digital" here: an eSIM has nothing to ship.

id.description: Session id, used in every follow-up call.

line_items.description: One entry per plan in the basket.

base_amount.description: Price of one unit, in minor units.

id.description: The plan id bought on this line.

links.description: Seller policies, for a buyer who asks.

messages.description: Anything the agent must read before completing: payment instructions, a gateway minimum this basket does not clear, or a warning that settlement is still pending.

content.description: The message itself. Payment instructions arrive here as fields (address, exact amount, memo): pass them through EXACTLY, never reformatted or rounded.

content_type.description: "application/json" when `content` is an object, "text/plain" when it is a sentence.

type.description: Whether this is information or a caution.

order.description: The order this session produced, once it has one. Null until then.

payment_handler_id.description: The handler this session will settle through.

price_locked_until.description: ISO 8601 timestamp until which these totals hold. After it, re-read the session for fresh totals rather than quoting these.

protocol.description: Agentic Commerce Protocol version this session speaks.

status.description: Where the session is: "ready_for_payment" means it can be completed; "complete_in_progress" means payment has not settled yet and the purchase is NOT done; "completed" means the eSIM is on its way. Also "incomplete", "not_ready_for_payment", "canceled" and "expired".

totals.description: The money, ordered so the lines read down to the total.

amount.description: Amount in minor units (cents) of the session currency. A discount is NEGATIVE, so the lines sum to the total.

display_text.description: The line written for a person.

description: Answer "which eSIM should I buy for this trip?". Give it the stops, a country code and the days spent in each, and it compares one plan covering the whole route against one plan per country against a mix of the two, on live prices, then flags the cheapest option that covers everything and explains the choice in a sentence you can quote. It also estimates the data each stop needs, names any country SimFuse cannot cover, and returns package ids that go straight into create-checkout-session. Use it whenever a trip has two or more countries, and for a single country when the traveller wants a recommendation rather than a list. Read-only: nothing is reserved and nothing is charged, and the totals are today's catalog prices, not a quote held for later.
